### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.git

### Question

Hi, 

I'm currently cutting down on my plugins. Besides moving what I can to mini I'm also creating my own statusbar, which is basically the nvim default one but with extra git information.

From what it seems, `mini.git` will show `HEAD` for the branch information when in detached head. I'd like to instead show the short commit instead. I know I could just get the full commit hash from `minigit_summary` and trim it but using something like `git rev-parse --short HEAD` would give me a "dynamic" sized short hash. In the codebases I work having 10 chars for the hash was not too uncommon.

Do you have an idea how I can achieve this? I know gitsigns does this by default, but it would be great if I could do this with mini instead.

This is what I currently have and it half works. But doing a `git checkout` I get spammed by errors and I'd also like for `Git rev-parse` to not open the result in a new buffer.

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
	pattern = "MiniGitUpdated",
	callback = function(data)
		local summary = vim.b[data.buf].minigit_summary
		if summary.head_name == "HEAD" then
			vim.cmd([[Git rev-parse --short HEAD]])
		end
	end
})

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', {
	pattern = "MiniGitCommandDone",
	callback = function(data)
		-- react on `:Git rev-parse`
		if data.data.git_subcommand == "rev-parse" then
			vim.b[data.buf].minigit_summary_string = data.data.stdout
		end
	end,
})
```

PS: To the reason for preferring the git hash over  `HEAD`, ... perhaps I convince you to make this a feature :)) 

I feel it gives me more information on where I am in my git tree. E.g if I'm backtracing commits for some faulty change and have my history open in a second window (github), I can map in my head what I see in the current buffer to the list I have open.
Also doing `git checkout <hash/branch>` and seeing the hash or branch name in the status line feels more consistent.

comment_data.body:
> From what it seems, `mini.git` will show `HEAD` for the branch information when in detached head.

Yes, [it is documented](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/d12b7c1b4dccc5245a3d2b7bc73da6dd910af2c0/doc/mini-git.txt#L421).

> I know I could just get the full commit hash from `minigit_summary` and trim it but using something like `git rev-parse --short HEAD` would give me a "dynamic" sized short hash. In the codebases I work having 10 chars for the hash was not too uncommon.

Yes, explicitly trimming full commit hash is the suggested approach and it is what is [done for `minigit_summary_string`](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/d12b7c1b4dccc5245a3d2b7bc73da6dd910af2c0/lua/mini/git.lua#L1468). If you feel like 10 characters is needed, then always trimming to 10 characters doesn't seem like a big problem.

> PS: To the reason for preferring the git hash over `HEAD`, ... perhaps I convince you to make this a feature :))

The main reason the `HEAD` is used to show detached head state is to be able to actually detect a detached HEAD state. If automatically replaced with commit hash, then there is no way to 100% detect the state (short commit hash can look very much like branch name).
